en: Now follows the hymn to Śani.

Śrī! Of this Śrī-Śanaiścara-stotra, Daśaratha is the seer (ṛṣi), Śanaiścara is the deity (devatā), Triṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), and its application (viniyoga) is in recitation for the sake of pleasing Śanaiścara.
Salutations to that son of the illustrious Sun, who is remembered as Koṇa, Antaka, Raudra, Yama, Babhru, Kṛṣṇa, Śani, Piṅgala, Manda, and Sauri, and who constantly removes all suffering. || 1 ||

The gods, asuras, kimpuruṣas, lords of the gaṇas, gandharvas, vidyādharas, and pannagas—all are tormented by him who stands in a precarious state; salutations to that son of the illustrious Sun. || 2 ||
Men and lords of men, beasts and lions, and those wild creatures such as insects, moths, and bees—all are tormented by him who stands in adversity; salutations to that son of the illustrious Sun.
Salutations to that son of the illustrious Sun, by whom all countries, fortresses, forests, military encampments, cities, and towns situated in difficult terrain are oppressed.

Through offerings of sesame, barley, beans, molasses, and rice, or by the gift of iron and blue garments, and by means of mantras on his own day, one pleases him; salutations to that son of the illustrious Sun.

Salutations to that son of the illustrious Sun, who is subtle even when absorbed in meditation by yogis at Prayāga, on the banks of the Yamunā, in the Sarasvatī of holy waters, and within the cave. || 6 ||

May that man who has entered his own home from another region on that [planet’s] day be happy. Salutations to him who, having departed from his house, does not return; salutations to the son of the illustrious Sun. 7.

The Self-born (Brahmā) is the creator of this universe; Hari is its protector; and the wielder of the Pināka bow (Śiva) withdraws it. He is one, yet threefold in the forms of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas. Homage to Him, the glorious son of the Sun! Homage! || 8 ||

He who, being self-restrained, daily recites the Śanyaṣṭaka at dawn, shall obtain happiness on earth accompanied by enjoyments through means of excellent sons, cattle, and kinsmen; he attains the supreme state of Nirvāṇa.
Situated in the corner is Piṅgala, Babhru, Kṛṣṇā, Raudrī, Antaka, Yama, Sauri, Śanaiścara, and Manda, who is praised by Pippalāda. || 10 ||
Whoever recites these ten names upon rising in the morning shall never experience affliction caused by Saturn. || 11 ||
Thus ends the Śanaiścara-stotra as proclaimed by the illustrious Daśaratha.
